svg.title: SpecSpec architecture: one graph, human and agent workflows
svg.desc: Read top to bottom. First, the owner enters through the shared VS Code or Electron visual workspace, and a coding agent enters through its own shell and the SpecSpec CLI. Their conversation takes place outside SpecSpec; built-in agent connectors are future work. The unprivileged renderer sends SpecSpecHost messages to authorized host adapters. GraphSession coordinates operations through a bounded, shell-free CLI bridge using argument arrays, UTF-8 stdin and API 5 JSON. The same Python library interprets canonical Markdown nodes, validates the rooted DAG, exports complete ancestor context, plans edits, resolves source regions and reads Git snapshots. Saved specifications live in _specspec; Git retains revisions and supplies exact staged blobs. The CLI reads saved files; VS Code working views also overlay open document text. File, document and Git notifications prompt coalesced rereads and render acknowledgements. Second, two persistence lanes distinguish journaled Python managed writes from non-writing Python plans applied to VS Code TextDocuments and persisted by native Save. Native Save can persist invalid text and has no Python lock or journal. Third, an agent working loop inspects owner changes and graph context, reasons about conclusions, implements and verifies, and returns to owner review. Deliberate staging and exact-index hook checks precede authorized commits. This is a descriptive overview, not an exhaustive call graph or an automated agent orchestration pipeline.
svg.metadata: Current format/API 5 implementation. Hand-authored offline SVG with literal text, system font fallbacks and local marker references only. Companion and source map: docs/architecture.md. Binding intentions and revisable conclusions: _specspec/ and docs/own-spec.md.

g.aria-label: Overview and visual key
g.text: A visual workspace for the owner. A CLI for the coding agent. Shared rules beneath both.

g.aria-label: Two entrances converge on one domain authority and canonical project files
g.text: The owner sees the graph. The agent asks the graph.

g.aria-label: Owner: browse, edit and review through the visual workspace
Owner-agent conversation is external to SpecSpec
One unprivileged canvas and narrow VS Code or Electron adapters
g.text: VS Code or Electron · one shared canvas

g.aria-label: Illustrative graph canvas

g.text: GraphSession · guarded queue · bounded CLI bridge
The canvas cannot access project files or spawn tools.
Host trust / authorization, dialogs and watchers stay in the adapters.

g.aria-label: Coding agent: call the CLI from its own shell, also available to people
g.text: impact · diff · sources · add · update · delete · validate

g.aria-label: Shell-free argument arrays and UTF-8 stdin go in; API 5 JSON, records and diagnostics come back
The CLI and reusable Python library own specification meaning, not the renderer
Canonical saved Markdown DAG, Git snapshots and linked product sources
One manifesto, multi-parent requirements and implementation leaves
Python reads files and Git snapshots; managed operations write files. Native saves are detailed in section two.

g.text: The CLI reads saved files. VS Code working views also overlay open text buffers; commit targets are read-only.

g.aria-label: Live feedback: events prompt coalesced rereads, snapshots and acknowledged canvas rendering
g.text: Invalid: marked last-valid view; drafts stay. Watchers are hints · polling off by default · explicit Refresh available.

g.aria-label: Same graph rules, different persistence lifecycles
g.text: Same graph rules. Different owners of Save.
A form is not a file. Follow the path for the host you use.

g.aria-label: CLI, Electron and VS Code project actions use Python's locked, journaled managed writer
g.text: Stage + journal → byte checks → replace / unlink
Delete previews all descendants (even shared children) + uncommitted warnings; reviewed scope is rechecked under lock.

g.aria-label: VS Code node-file forms use non-writing Python plans, WorkspaceEdit, native TextDocuments and native Save; raw edits go straight to the buffer
g.text: Raw edits go straight to this buffer
Native Save may persist invalid text. Managed project mutations require clean SpecSpec documents.
Manual Markdown edits are allowed. Cameras, colors and view state stay outside the canonical specification.

g.aria-label: Recommended agent working loop and deliberate exact-index validation before authorized commits
g.text: Agent work returns to owner judgment.
Recommended workflow, not an automated product pipeline.

g.aria-label: Inspect owner edits and read complete ancestor context
Reason about intentions and deepen independently revisable conclusions
Implement and maintain source and verification links
Validate, compare and return bounded evidence to the owner

g.text: git add → specspec hook check [--sources] → git commit
The hook checks exact staged blobs. SpecSpec never stages or commits for you; hook installation is opt-in.
